original_test_intent: Physically assess DC-SCM serviceability and seating, perform one approved plug/unplug cycle, and confirm after recovery/reboot that the identical SCM and affected management/device functions are detected without new errors.
original_method: A trained operator records the exact DC-SCM and slot, photos and management baseline, establishes ESD and required power isolation, removes/reseats the module once per service procedure, restores connectors/retention/chassis, performs the approved reboot, and compares BMC, host, device, driver/link and error evidence to baseline.
manual_activity: A trained operator physically inspects, removes and reseats the identified DC-SCM, restores all retention/connections and observes recovery; the owner reviews physical and management/system evidence.
required_inputs: SUT/chassis, exact DC-SCM FRU/serial/revision and slot/connector/retention/cable map
Approved DC-SCM service procedure, permitted cycle count, power-state and ESD requirements
Pre/post BMC/host/module identity, firmware/driver/link and error acceptance criteria
Independent console/management recovery path and hardware service escalation plan
Camera/evidence labeling, operator identity and no-log-clear policy
safety_requirements: Only a trained operator may handle DC-SCM under the approved ESD and power-safe procedure
Do not remove or insert the module energized unless the service procedure explicitly authorizes that exact operation
Stop on wrong FRU/slot, bent pins, connector/retention damage, excessive force, unexpected power state, loss of management/boot or new hardware error
Perform one approved cycle only and diagnose before any repeat
Restore connectors, latches, screws, cables and chassis closure before power/reboot
agent_execution_scope: Verify row-2003 variant identity and prepare the DC-SCM evidence checklist
Collect and compare pre/post BMC/host inventory, firmware, driver/link state and unfiltered logs around the operator action
Organize photos, physical-action timeline, recovery events and output hashes
Flag identity changes, management loss, missing detection or incomplete physical evidence
Perform no physical manipulation, visual seating verdict, reboot authorization or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve exact DC-SCM/slot, service sequence, safe state, cycle count and recovery plan
Ensure trained operator completes the physical inspection/reseat and signs the evidence
Review pre/post management, device and physical changes and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The NO decision is correct because remote commands cannot manipulate or visually judge the DC-SCM. They can only corroborate identity, management recovery and error state before and after.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use project-approved read-only BMC/host inventory, module firmware, device/driver/link and log commands before and after the operator's one physical cycle; exact commands depend on the DC-SCM architecture.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: DC-SCM scope, plug/unplug and post-cycle detection intent, seating criterion and 5/5-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL MANUAL PHYSICAL DC-SCM RESEAT VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed module/slot checklist with before/after photos, ESD/power confirmation, one-cycle timeline and correlated BMC/host management, inventory, driver/link and error evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds SCM-specific identity, management recovery and safety controls without automating the essential physical judgment.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A responding BMC or inventory entry cannot prove connector condition or full seating; physical inspection plus pre/post management and device evidence are both required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: DC-SCM removal can eliminate management access or strand the platform. Remote evidence may disappear precisely when the module is mis-seated, so an independent recovery path is essential.

project_override_considerations: If this DC-SCM supports live replacement, the exact platform hot-service sequence and management handoff must be supplied; otherwise use approved power isolation. Do not import the row-2006 CX8 Board process or Mellanox criteria.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash plus DC-SCM FRU/serial/revision, slot, connectors, retention/cables and service-procedure revision
Operator identity, ESD/power-safe confirmation and labeled before/after photos
Pre/post BMC/host/module inventory, firmware, driver/link, reboot/recovery timeline and unfiltered errors
One-cycle/no-repeat/no-log-clear audit, restored hardware state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The row consistently targets DC-SCM physical cycling, detection and seating. The shared code is an identity hazard, but row 2003 and its hash uniquely select the module variant.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case is MANUAL ONLY, not globally blocked. Physical access, trained operator, service procedure and recovery controls are execution prerequisites while static review is complete.

review_improvement: Binds the shared code to the DC-SCM variant and makes loss-of-management recovery and module identity explicit in the physical cycle evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: DC-SCM may host or mediate management functions, so a reseat can remove the very telemetry used for remote confirmation. That makes an independent console/recovery route and pre-action identity capture essential. Successful post-reboot detection does not prove connector or latch condition, while visual seating alone cannot prove management/device recovery. Both evidence domains must agree, and the unrelated same-code CX8 Board variant must remain isolated.
